about: drawn after franka.de's product render and Franka Research 3 photos (2026-11-12): the white satin shell, the brushed aluminium inlay strips, the turned aluminium flange, the milled aluminium fingers, the black plug and cable, the black rubber pad (the Library's part).  The screws are the project's own drawing, not the model's, as plain cylinders.  On each finger's outer face: two socket-head screws in their counterbores (where the model keeps two closed pockets inside the finger's solid, unseen) and the fingertip's screw, drawn once in the finger's frame and standing on both fingers (bodies/franka-hand/drawn-screws.stl and drawn-screw-bores.stl).  On the one broad face of the shell that the photos show (the plug on the right when the flange is up): the two small screws beside the inlay strip, on the fingers' side of it, 3.5 mm from its edge, a third and two thirds along it, their places read from the photos to about 2 mm (drawn-shell-screws.stl in drawn-shell-screw-seats.stl).  The other broad face is in no photo, so nothing is drawn on it.  No guide rail, lettering or pad groove is modelled.

shell-white.evidence: the FR3 photos and the product render: the shell reads #cfcfd7 to #eeeeee on every face; at the homes its broad face is turned from the key, so it takes more of the studio's light under a base colour a little darker: #cdd0d4 there under a #eef0f3 top (the base look: a brighter top, lost in the card's ground)

inlay-brushed.evidence: the FR3 close-up (the AI Companion photo): lengthwise brush lines on the strip, a wide streaked highlight, #8a8d94 to #9c9fa6 beside a #cfcfd7 shell; #a8a8a9 beside #dbdbdc in the two-arm photo, #c1c1c1 beside #e3e3e3 in the product render: a grey clearly darker than the shell.  At the homes the strip mirrors the room below the camera, so its reflections are lifted: it reads #a6a9ad there beside the shell's #cfd1d5 (at 2 it read #bfc2c7, nearly the shell's grey).  A quarter turn to the left that face is turned to the key and strip and shell are both the card's white (#f5f8fc on #eff1f4), as the strip is in the high-key photo (#e1e1e1 beside #e9e9e9); less of a mirror (metalness 0.4 to 0.65 with a darker colour) reads #e5e9ee to #ecf0f5 there once the homes' grey is kept, and loses the gradient from behind, so it is not taken

flange-turned.evidence: the product render and the FR3 photos: a turned flange plate with fine concentric tool marks, mirror-like next to the satin fingers

bore-dark.evidence: the product render: the fingers' counterbores and the screws' sockets read #2a2b2d, dark rings round silver heads; the FR3 photos: the shell's screws sit in darker seats

screw-bright.evidence: the FR3 photos (the AI Companion close-up, the two-arm photo, the high-key one): the shell's small screws are even light silver dots, about #b4b6b9, a little darker than the white face round them; in the high-key photo a light head in a dark ring.  A 3 mm flat head of the base steel mirrors one patch of the room: #76797b at the homes, where the face is turned from the key, and with its reflections lifted (1.6) #989b9e at the homes but #5b5d5f an eighth of a turn to the left and #7e8184 beside #a1a4a7 a sixth of a turn to the left and up.  So the heads are less of a mirror: #a6a9ad at the homes beside the shell's #cfd1d5, #999ca0 to #9ca0a3 and #b8bbbf to #c2c5c9 in those two views.  A quarter turn to the left, the face turned to the key, the heads are the shell's white (#eef1f5 beside #f0f2f5) and only their dark seats show
